correctness.rationale: Jacobi complementary minors give label probabilities p_i=G_ii/tr(G); exact minimization fixes x_i and yields x^+=x_i Ge_i/G_ii. The second-moment transition Q_{ji}=p_j G_ij^2/G_ii^2 is diagonal-similar to K_ij=G_ij^2/(tr(G) sqrt(G_ii G_jj)); Schur positivity and Perron comparison prove r in (0,1), the positive all-coordinate start guarantees positive leading coefficient even when K reducible. A zero inverse-Hessian offdiagonal yields a positive-probability annihilating adjacent label pair almost surely; if all entries nonzero, telescoped scale ratios and finite-state ergodic SLLN yield gamma=sum p_i p_j log|C_ij|, negative since SPD strict correlations. Independently tested 2240 rational/numerical path-update identities over 40 SPD matrices; no finite test substituted for spectral/SLLN proofs.
residual_risks: Only deterministic x0 with all coordinates nonzero supports the sharp coefficient/nonabsorption conclusions; exact arithmetic and independent labels are necessary.

value.rationale: This quantifies two different natural notions of convergence for a real determinant-volume optimization algorithm and gives a sharp inverse-Hessian structural criterion for finite termination, neither merely a routine estimator bound nor an arbitrary slice.
residual_risks: Does not establish floating-point finite termination or practical runtime superiority.

final_claim: For maximal (n-1)-coordinate determinant-volume sampling of a fixed SPD quadratic, exact mean-square Perron decay, inverse-Hessian-zero absorption dichotomy, and dense-inverse almost-sure Lyapunov exponent hold with the stated positive-coordinate initial condition.
